findings.title: Debris, Return, and the Appointed Term
findings.claim: 17:97 places the rejecting group in an inverted bodily state and a fire that repeatedly revives; 17:98 voices the objection of bones and fragments, and 17:99 answers that the creator can make their like and has set a certain term. The pericope holds bodily ruin, return, and renewed intensity together.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the power to create their like, the appointed term, and the refusal that closes the ayah. The triggers are 17:97's gathering on faces and fire that abates only to be increased, followed by 17:98's bones, scattered remains, and question about being raised as a new creation. Their contact changes the creation claim from an abstract proof into a reply to bodily fragmentation, placed beside continuing consequence; the appointed term supplies a temporal bound.
findings.reader_payoff: The answer addresses the very material image raised by the objection: fragments can be met with renewed creation, while the appointed term and recurring fire make this a bounded, consequential future event.
findings.containment: 17:98 leaves open whether the returned beings are numerically the same persons or an equivalent human kind. The fire cycle and the appointed term are adjacent pericope images; they are not equated. The focus claim remains that God can create their like and has set a doubtless term.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel nomination lands on exact focus and supplied context occurrences. Its dispatch image is a nominated branch and remains a bounded contextual analogy; the relation does not decide personal identity.

findings.title: Seeing Beside Closed Faculties
findings.claim: The preceding portrait of people gathered blind, mute, and deaf places the focus's challenge to see within an image of closed faculties. The focus's refusal then reads as resistance to the evidence those faculties could receive.
findings.mechanism: Before the context, the opening can read as a question merely asking people to inspect creation. 17:97 supplies blindness, muteness, and deafness; the focus supplies seeing, strong refusal, and kufur. Their contact changes the question into a challenge against sensory and rational closure already pictured in the gathering, while refusal names the response to that challenge.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the focus's seeing as inward recognition as well as sight, and can perceive refusal as a response to evidence rather than a purely abstract decision.
findings.containment: The HFT trace itself allows 17:97 to describe only the manner of eschatological gathering. The finding does not identify those gathered there with every wrongdoer in 17:99; the focus still asks whether they recognize creation.

epistemic.reason: Every HFT word index and root matches the supplied focus or 17:97 context occurrence. The context branch records remain lexically unresolved, so their role is retained as attributed evidence with the HFT alternative visible.

The focus carrier قَادِرٌ meets 17:100's finite stock, blocked outflow, and narrowing of provision, while كُفُورًا names refusal to acknowledge an unwithheld gift. That contact changes the question from power's size alone to the human model of power as something exhausted by giving.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that the doubt about renewed creation may expose the limits of a creaturely economy: people withhold because they imagine resources running out, while the focus predicates capability of the creator.
findings.containment: 17:100 may address generosity without commenting on resurrection reasoning. The scarcity projection is an attributed contextual analogy, not a stated cause of every refusal.

epistemic.reason: All five HFT trace roots and word indices match 17:99 or the lean 17:100 context. The before/after shift is retained as an attributed inference, with the HFT's alternative about generosity preserved.

findings.title: Recognized Signs Recast as Deception
findings.claim: 17:101-102 places manifest signs, knowledge, and inner insight beside Pharaoh's accusation of magic and hostile conjecture. This makes the focus's no-doubt claim and kufur readable as resistance that relabels disclosed evidence; the focus's challenge to see can also resonate with considered judgment beside Pharaoh's own conjecture.
findings.mechanism: Before these ayat, kufur can read as a bare rejection after an argument. The pericope shows signs made manifest, knowledge already admitted, inward insight, and an accusation that redescribes the signs as magic. The focus's negated doubt and religious refusal meet that sequence; yaraw's judgment facet meets the later aẓunnu conjecture. The contact changes refusal into an active counter-labeling operation while preserving the ordinary challenge to recognize creation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive how evidence may be present and even acknowledged while a hostile description gives refusal a way to continue.
findings.containment: The HFT alternative remains live: Pharaoh's accusations may be political tactics rather than inward concealment. This is a pericope example, not proof of every wrongdoer's motive or a replacement of the focus's primary refusal.

epistemic.reason: Every HFT trace coordinate matches the supplied 17:101-102 root occurrences or focus QAC. The additional opinion facet is a bounded branch activation from the exact contrast between yaraw and aẓunnu; HFT roles and its political-tactic alternative remain visible.

findings.title: An Appointed Horizon of Displacement and Gathering
findings.claim: The focus's created earth and appointed term stand beside Pharaoh's attempted expulsion, his drowning, restored habitation, and a promised later assembly. The focus's plural wrongdoer label can also resonate with the pericope's concrete act of moving people from their rightful place.
findings.mechanism: Before 17:103-104, the term can read as an individual deadline attached to renewed creation. The context makes earth the site of attempted removal and restored dwelling; drowning reverses the aggressor's act, while a later promise gathers mixed groups. The focus's earth, assigning verb, and appointed term meet these events, and the registered wrongdoer facet meets the attempted displacement. The term thus becomes a governed horizon for reversal and gathering without being equated with the context's separate promise.
findings.reader_payoff: The creator's power is seen operating in lived history: an attempted uprooting is reversed, a people are told to dwell in the land, and a later assembly is bounded by a promise.
findings.containment: The historical sequence may illustrate power without specifying the referent of the focus's appointed term. The groups are not identified with one another, and 17:104's promise is not asserted to be the same event as 17:99's term.

epistemic.reason: The HFT's focus/context roots and indices match the supplied 17:99, 17:103, and 17:104 occurrences. Its analogy remains attributed; the wrongful-displacement facet is independently available and is tied to the exact expulsion trigger without identifying the actors.

findings.title: A Certain Term Within Measured Process
findings.claim: 17:105-106's true descent, division into parts, deliberate interval, and repeated delivery allow the appointed term in 17:99 to be read within certain but paced administration: unfolding over time need not imply hesitation.
findings.mechanism: Before this context, the term can appear as a single remote deadline whose delay invites doubt. The focus supplies an appointed duration with no doubt; 17:105 names true delivery, and 17:106 divides the recitation for deliberate reading and repeats its descent. Their contact changes the term into one instance of measured administration, where certainty and interval coexist.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus's certainty as compatible with a process that unfolds by stages and intervals.
findings.containment: The contextual relation remains an analogy: staged revelation may not characterize the appointed term beyond their shared involvement with time. The 17:106 connection row records no material addition and its reciprocal note calls this route remote; that counter-signal remains live. The HFT relation is retained as attributed evidence, not as identity between recitation and the term.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT coordinates match the 17:99, 17:105, and 17:106 occurrences. The connection row is contrary evidence rather than a filter; retaining this trace as a qualified analogy preserves both the HFT change and the supplied counter-signal.

findings.title: Refusal and the Body That Yields
findings.claim: 17:107 and 17:109 show hearers falling to their chins in prostration and humility when recitation reaches them; beside 17:99's refusal, the pericope gives opposed bodily postures for response to signs.
findings.mechanism: Before this context, refusal can read as an abstract decision not to accept an argument. The focus carries forceful refusal and religious rejection; the later recitation, repeated falling, prostration, and humility supply an embodied response. Their contact changes the refusal into one posture within a contrast between resisting and yielding to recitation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive response to revelation in bodily action: the focus names refusal, while the later ayat show recognition lowering the body.
findings.containment: The groups may be distinct, and the later scene may function as an independent commendation rather than a direct foil. The focus's refusal remains intelligible on its own.

epistemic.reason: Every HFT context coordinate and root matches the selected 17:107 and 17:109 word occurrences; the before/after change is retained as attributed posture contrast with the source's alternative intact.

findings.title: Creaturely Likeness Beside Sovereignty
findings.claim: The focus's claim that God can create human likeness stands beside 17:111's denials of offspring and shared dominion. The pericope bounds the likeness as creaturely correspondence, not a relation that makes the creator a child, counterpart, or co-owner.
findings.mechanism: Before 17:111, 'their like' can be heard as an unrestricted duplication. The focus names Allah as creator, creates the human counterpart, and marks similarity; the closing ayah denies offspring and partnership in dominion, then magnifies God. These carriers and triggers preserve the creator-creature asymmetry while allowing human likeness to remain.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold renewed human resemblance together with the focus's distinction between creator and creature.
findings.containment: The focus's pronoun already points to humans, and 17:111 may close the surah independently. This contextual boundary does not claim that mithl refers to God or that the focus's wording is ambiguous.

epistemic.reason: The seven exact HFT trace roles match the 17:99 focus words and 17:111 context indices. Context branch records are unresolved and remain attributed; the alternative that 17:111 is an independent close is preserved.

findings.title: Heavens as a Sign Beside the Divine Names
findings.claim: The focus's visible heavens can echo 17:110's beautiful names: the act of seeing creation may carry perception from the high visible object toward the creator who is named.
findings.mechanism: Before the context, the heavens function as evidence of scale. The focus's seeing and heavens meet the distinct naming branch in 17:110; the shared root across the two words supplies a branch-sensitive echo, and the later names direct attention toward the named creator.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice a local wordplay that lets the cosmic object be seen as an indication, while keeping sky and name as distinct meanings.
findings.containment: The source explicitly bounds this as resonance or wordplay, not one etymological meaning for sky and name. It remains an exploratory, attributed contact; the focus's ordinary heavens and the later invocation remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 17:110 word/root coordinates match the supplied packet. The relation is explicitly bounded as an attributed branch-sensitive echo, with no etymological collapse.
